Theme

Body, health & movement

clear your throat verb

also hawk, hem, cough up phlegm

classical

Plaut. Curc. 117: tibi quī screantī, siccae, sēmisomnae

screō, screāre

verb, first conjugation

hawk, hem, clear the throat

(vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

Its noun is screātus, screātūs (Ter. Heaut. 373).

Other words

  • exscreō, exscreāre — hawk up, cough up

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cels. 4.6: per tussim exscreātur … pītuīta (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Asin. 1.1.27: age, age, ūsque excreā (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Gemitūs, screātūs, tussīs, rīsūs abstinē.

    No groaning, no clearing your throat, no coughing, no laughing.Ter. Heaut. 373

See also cough, spit out, throat.

SourcesLewis & Short: screo · Lewis & Short: exscreo

Plautus, Curculio 117. Terence, Heautontimorumenos 373.
